title: Strong SetDisjointness conjecture
formal: Is the following statement true? For every admissible uniform static word-RAM data structure for SetDisjointness, with worst-case retained space \(S(N)\) words and worst-case query time \(T(N)\) steps, there exist constants \(c>0\), \(b\in\mathbb N\), and \(N_0\ge2\) such that \(S(N)T(N)^2\ge cN^2/(\log_2(N+2))^b\) for every integer \(N\ge N_0\). For every integer \(N\ge2\), the input is a list \(A_1,\ldots,A_m\) of nonempty subsets of \([N]=\{1,\ldots,N\}\), with \(1\le m\le N\) and total size \(N=\sum_{i=1}^m|A_i|\). A query supplies indices \(i,j\in[m]\) and must return whether \(A_i\cap A_j=\varnothing\).
definitions:
The input gives \(N\), \(m\), the lengths of the sets, and each set's elements explicitly as words, without repetitions within a set. Different listed sets may be equal. The indices of two stored sets are the whole query; there is no new query set. The case \(i=j\) is allowed. Each admissible data structure is a fixed pair of finite programs, one for preprocessing and one for queries, working for every input size. The word length is \(w=\lceil10\log_2(N+2)\rceil\). The sequential word RAM has word-sized registers and addressed memory cells; each read, write, comparison, branch, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero integer, Boolean bit operation, or logical shift costs one step. Arithmetic stored in a word is modulo \(2^w\), and a shift by at least \(w\) returns zero. Addresses fit in one word. Outputting the answer and all memory operations are charged.

Preprocessing must halt on every valid input and random execution, but its finite running time is unrestricted. Only the resulting stored representation is accessible to a query; the original input is not available for free. The representation includes all retained input-dependent tables, seeds, pointers and metadata. A query begins with its two indices, the input-size metadata and that representation, with no input-dependent private state inherited from earlier queries. It leaves the representation unchanged. Temporary query storage starts empty; accessing or filling it costs time. There is no advice, oracle, input-specific code, or uncharged precomputed table.

The two programs may generate independent uniformly random words in one step. For every fixed input and fixed valid query, the probability of the correct empty/nonempty answer, over preprocessing randomness and independent query randomness, is at least \(2/3\). The query bound holds for every random outcome, including erroneous ones. Let \(s(N)\) be the maximum retained word count over all valid inputs of total size exactly \(N\) and preprocessing outcomes, and let \(T(N)\ge1\) be the maximum query step count over those inputs, their produced representations, all valid queries and all query outcomes. These maxima are required to be finite. Use the saved card's space normalization \(S(N)=\max\{N,s(N)\}\), and restrict to structures with \(S(N)\le N^2\). Unused cells may be padded. All constants in the asserted bound may depend on the fixed programs, but not on \(N\), the input family, or the query. The displayed bound is the precise meaning of \(S(N)T(N)^2=\widetilde\Omega(N^2)\); it suppresses only fixed powers of a logarithm, not an arbitrary \(N^{o(1)}\) factor.
why: This conjecture underlies many space-query conditional lower bounds for text indexes, graph oracles and set systems.

context_blocks.text: Goldstein, Kopelowitz, Lewenstein and Porat formulate the Strong SetDisjointness conjecture as \(S=\widetilde\Omega(N^2/T^2)\). Their \(N\) is total set incidence count, not the number of sets. The source explicitly uses the tilde notation to suppress polylogarithmic factors.

A matching upper tradeoff has retained space \(O(N+N^2/t^2)\) words and query time \(O(t)\), in particular \(S T^2=O(N^2)\) in the relevant range \(1\le t\le\sqrt N\). This upper bound does not establish the conjectured universal lower bound.

The 2020 algorithms of Kopelowitz and Vassilevska Williams improve the tradeoff between preprocessing time and query time. Their analysis measures preprocessing time separately from retained storage, so its improved preprocessing bound does not refute this space-query conjecture.

Huang, Tao and Wang use the same space-query conjecture in their 2026 work on join sampling, in a word-RAM with logarithmic word length. Their Lemma 21 relates an expected-query-time formulation for exact answers to the formulation with deterministic query time. They assume the conjecture rather than prove its lower bound.

This review retains the card's explicitly chosen uniform, bounded-error word-RAM convention and normalized space range. The 2017 conjecture itself does not spell out these machine, uniformity and error details. Relabelling the elements of the union into \([N]\) preserves every intersection; empty sets and self-pair queries are trivial.

The Strong 3SUM-Indexing conjecture mentioned alongside SetDisjointness in the original paper was subsequently refuted. The 2019 bounded-universe paper explicitly distinguishes that development and continues to assume Strong SetDisjointness for its conditional results.

progress.text: The source proposes the full \(S T^2=\widetilde\Omega(N^2)\) lower-bound conjecture and records its matching upper tradeoff.
The bounded-universe results assume Strong SetDisjointness. The paper separately records that the stronger 3SUM-indexing conjecture has been refuted.
Improved algorithms address the preprocessing-time/query-time tradeoff, while retaining the distinction between preprocessing work and stored space.
The join-sampling paper still uses Strong SetDisjointness as a conjecture and proves a transfer to its expected-query-time variant for exact answers.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the displayed universal lower bound or its logical negation in the specified model. A refutation must violate every admissible polylogarithmic lower-bound factor for one fixed admissible data structure; a fixed logarithmic improvement alone is not a refutation. The negation is an asymptotic assertion and need not have a finite counterexample. Results conditional on Strong SetDisjointness, or lower bounds only for preprocessing time, do not establish this lower bound.
status_note: Strong SetDisjointness is conjectured in the 2017 source and is still assumed in the checked ICDT 2026 paper. The bounded primary-source review on 16 September 2026 found no matching proof or refutation of the saved bounded-error word-RAM target; later use of the conjecture is not an exhaustive current-status certificate.

sentences: A family of sets is stored before the queries arrive.
Each query names two stored sets and asks whether their intersection is empty.
The conjecture says that retained space times squared query time cannot beat the squared total input size by more than polylogarithmic factors.
Known upper bounds attain that tradeoff, while recent work still uses its lower-bound direction as an assumption.
Preprocessing time is unrestricted and remains a separate resource from retained storage.

previous.formal: Is it true that every static word-RAM data structure for SetDisjointness with space \(S(N)\) and worst-case query time \(T(N)\) satisfies \(S(N)T(N)^2=\widetilde\Omega(N^2)\)? The input is a list of nonempty sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\subseteq[N]\) with total size \(N=\sum_i|S_i|\), and a query \((i,j)\) asks whether \(S_i\cap S_j\) is empty.
previous.definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. The sets are supplied as lists without repeated elements within a set, with \(m\le N\) and \(N\ge2\). Word size is \(w=\lceil10\log_2(N+2)\rceil\). Restrict attention to \(N\le S(N)\le N^2\), rounding up and padding unused cells if needed. Preprocessing may use arbitrary finite time; all input-dependent information retained afterwards counts toward \(S(N)\). A query reads this static representation and begins without input-dependent private state. Randomized preprocessing and query algorithms are allowed; the answer to each fixed input/query must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). Space and query time bounds hold for every random outcome. The notation means that, for each admissible data structure, there are constants \(c>0\), \(b\ge0\), and \(N_0\) such that \(S(N)T(N)^2\ge cN^2/(\log(2+N))^b\) for all \(N\ge N_0\). All sizes are measured in words and time in word-RAM steps. Uniform programs and exact empty/nonempty semantics are required; reporting the intersection is another problem.
